newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini sees ERM re-entry soon.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini sees ERM re-entry soon.

text.p: Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Friday that he expected the lira to return soon to Europe's exchange rate grid, which it crashed out of in September 1992.
"It will not be long before Italy is in the ERM again," Dini said in an interview for Reuters Financial Television in Naples, where he is among ministers attending an Italian-French summit.
Asked whether he thought the lira would return to the ERM by the end of this year, Dini said: "Soon, but I don't know because this is a matter the treasury ministers are discussing".
The run-up to the summit with France was marred by renewed criticism by French President Jacques Chirac of the weakness in the lira, which he blames for hurting French industry.
His spokeswoman has said France wants a rapid lira return to the ERM but only after it has appreciated further.

The lira lost around 40 percent of its value after being ejected from the ERM but has since regained some 20 percent and stood in late New York trading at 991.85 to the German mark, slightly off its 27-month high reached earlier in the day.
